Methaemoglobinaemia has been re- ported with several local anaesthetics including tetracaine,1 ben- zocaine,1-5 and lidocaine1,6 but is more commonly associated with the use of prilocaine.7-10 It may occur after local injection or topical use. It has been suggested that the effect is due to the pres- ence of an aniline group in the structure or, in the case of lido- caine and prilocaine, metabolism to an aniline-like structure. Methaemoglobinaemia may result from the use of usual doses as well as exposure to toxic concentrations of local anaesthetic;1,9 with prilocaine doses of 8 mg/kg or more [above recommended maxima] usually produce symptoms.11 Table 1.
